title: Market/Disposition Event
description: A detected real-world event that explains why a batch of assets is coming to market at a given price, e.g. a rental fleet refresh, a bankruptcy auction, or a natural disaster driving generator demand. The thesis this schema encodes: the event that created a sale is often a bigger driver of pricing dislocation than the specific brand/model — this is the structured 'why is it mispriced' record nothing else in the schema set captures.

region.description: Same shape as regional_demand.region — reused rather than redefined so the two can be joined directly.

category.description: Controlled vocabulary term, see taxonomy.schema.json. Null if the event isn't category-specific (e.g. an interest_rate_shock).

confidence.description: Confidence the detected event is real and correctly typed, not a confidence in its price impact.

source_signal.description: Free-text description of what triggered detection, e.g. 'court filing docket match', 'dealer inventory age spike + surplus listing spike in region'.

linked_listing_ids.description: Listings attributed to this event. See also listing.source.market_event_ref for the inverse FK.

linked_transaction_ids.description: sold_transaction records attributed to this event. See also sold_transaction.source.market_event_ref for the inverse FK.
